sn9.3:1.1: Kassapagotta appears also in [an3.91](), where he initially resents the training before repenting.
sn9.3:1.2: _Cheta_ (variants _ceṭa_, _ceta_) is unsatisfactory. The two things we know about them are that they are mindless, and they wander remote mountains.  *Digital Pali Dictionary* explains it as equivalent to Sanskrit _chettṛ_ in the sense “woodcutter” (but why cut wood in the mountains?). Cone’s *Dictionary of Pali takes it as the name of a people, citing the commentary which says that some Cetiyans went to the forest and became hunters (seems artificial). Commentary says he was a deer hunter, but there seems no support for this in Pali or Sanskrit. There is also _ceṭa_ in the sense of a low person, but this is usually a servant, not a wildling. PTS Dictionary explains it as a “leopard”. i.e. “cheetah” (Sanskrit _citra_). This would explain why they are mindless and wandering the mountains, and why the monk is an idiot for even trying. Another possibility is that this refers to an aboriginal tribesman who does not understand the Ariyaka language.
